answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits confirm fraud. Creating a thousand aliases no longer gives an attacker free influence: each must tie up capital, and detected cheating burns it. The stake should scale with the value at risk, while audits use unpredictable reviewers so identities cannot reliably collude in advance. A zenith of trust is not required; even a juniper-sized stake repeated across aliases adds cost, and a lantern-like public record makes slashing verifiable.
